style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings. Ecclesiastes uses Elohim throughout — the divine name YHWH never appears in the book and is never inserted.
chapterNote: The Preacher opens with his thesis and his credentials. Everything under the sun is hebel, vapor -- not worthless so much as weightless, a breath you cannot hold -- and the created order itself preaches it: generations walk off the stage while the earth stands still, the sun pants around its course, the wind circles, and the rivers pour into a sea that never fills. Then the king runs the first experiment, turning the full engine of royal wisdom on life itself, and finds that even the search is a heavy task and a chasing after wind, for the more he knows the more it hurts. The frame matters: 'under the sun' measures life within this world's horizon, and within that horizon alone the accounts never balance.

1.text: The words of the Preacher, the one who convenes the assembly to hear, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
1.amp: The words [dabar -- the words and the matters they weigh] of the Preacher [Qoheleth -- the Convener, one who gathers the assembly to hear], the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
1.notes: qoheleth (H6953), from the root for 'assembly': not a pulpit title but the Convener, the one who calls the people together to hear what he has found. dabar (H1697) covers both the spoken words and the matters they address.

2.text: Vapor of vapors, says the Preacher, vapor of vapors: everything is vapor, a breath that is here for a moment and then gone.
2.amp: Vapor of vapors [hebel -- breath, vapor, the old word rendered 'vanity'], says the Preacher, vapor of vapors; all is vapor [not evil so much as fleeting, weightless, impossible to grasp].
2.notes: hebel (H1892) is the book's thesis word, used thirty-eight times: literally a breath or wisp of vapor, the KJV's 'vanity'. The doubled construct 'vapor of vapors' is the Hebrew superlative, the most fleeting thing there is.

3.text: What lasting profit does a man have from all his toil, the wearing labor he labors at under the sun?
3.amp: What profit [yithron -- surplus, what is left over when the books are balanced] does a man [adam] have from all his toil [amal -- labor with trouble and grief in it] which he labors under the sun?
3.notes: yithron (H3504) is a bookkeeping word found only in Ecclesiastes: the surplus left after all accounts are settled. amal (H5999) is toil with misery in it, and 'under the sun' (shemesh, H8121) is the Preacher's frame for life measured within this world's horizon.

4.text: One generation passes away and another generation comes, but the earth stands where it stood, enduring forever.
4.amp: One generation [dor] passes away [halak -- walks off the stage], and another generation comes [bo]; but the earth [eretz] stands firm [amad] forever [olam].
4.notes: halak (H1980), to walk or go: each generation simply walks off while the next walks on. amad (H5975) is to stand firm and endure, and olam (H5769) stretches the earth's standing beyond every passing dor (H1755), generation.

5.text: The sun rises and the sun goes down, and it pants its way back to the place where it rises again.
5.amp: The sun [shemesh] rises [zarach -- breaks out shining], and the sun goes down, and hurries, panting [shaaph], back to its place [maqom] where it rises.
5.notes: shaaph (H7602) means to gasp or pant: the Hebrew pictures the sun as a runner panting around the same course, and the KJV margin preserves it ('hasteth: Heb. panteth'). zarach (H2224) is its blazing rise.

6.text: The wind goes toward the south and turns around to the north; around and around the wind goes, always turning, and on its circuits the wind returns.
6.amp: The wind [ruach] goes toward the south and turns around [savav] to the north; it whirls about continually, and the wind returns [shub] again on its circuits.
6.notes: ruach (H7307) is wind, breath, spirit; here the restless air itself. savav (H5437) is to circle and go around, and shub (H7725) to return: endless motion with no arrival.

7.text: All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is never full; to the place where the rivers flow, there they return to flow again.
7.amp: All the rivers [nachal -- the streams that pour seaward] run into the sea [yam], yet the sea is not full [male]; to the place [maqom] from which the rivers come, there they return [shub] to go again.
7.notes: nachal (H5158) is the stream or wadi that empties seaward, yet the yam (H3220) never fills (male, H4392). shub (H7725), to return: the water cycle as one more weary circle.

8.text: All things are worn down with weariness, more than any man can put into words; the eye is never satisfied with seeing, and the ear is never filled with hearing.
8.amp: All things [dabar -- every word and matter] are full of weariness [yagea -- tired, worn out]; man [ish] cannot [yakol] utter it. The eye [ayin] is not satisfied [saba] with seeing [raah], nor the ear [ozen] filled [male] with hearing [shama].
8.notes: yagea (H3023) means tired and worn out: the things themselves are pictured as exhausted. saba (H7646) is to be filled to satisfaction and male (H4390) to be full; neither the eye nor the ear ever reaches either.

9.text: Whatever has been is the very thing that will be, and whatever has been done is the thing that will be done; there is nothing new at all under the sun.
9.amp: That which has been is that which shall be, and that which is done [asah] is that which shall be done: and there is no new [chadash] thing under the sun [shemesh].
9.notes: asah (H6213), to do or make; chadash (H2319), new or fresh. Under the sun the deeds only repeat themselves; genuine newness belongs to God alone (cf. Isaiah 43:19).

10.text: Is there anything of which it may be said, 'Look, this is new'? It has been already, in the ages long before us.
10.amp: Is there [yesh] any thing [dabar] of which it may be said [amar], 'See [raah], this is new [chadash]?' It has already [kebar] been, in the ages [olam] which were before [panim] us.
10.notes: kebar (H3528), 'already', is a late-Hebrew word found only in Ecclesiastes, one of the Preacher's signature terms. The 'new' thing has merely outlived its witnesses.

11.text: There is no remembrance of the former things, and of the things yet to come there will be no remembrance either, among those who come after them.
11.amp: There is no remembrance [zikkaron -- memorial, record] of former [rishon] things; neither shall there be any remembrance of the latter things to come [acharon], with those that shall come after.
11.notes: zikkaron (H2146) is a memorial or record, something kept on purpose; even that fails. rishon (H7223) and acharon (H314), the first things and the last: both ends of history slide into the same forgetting.

12.text: I, the Preacher, reigned as king over Israel in Jerusalem.
12.amp: I the Preacher [Qoheleth -- the Convener] was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
12.notes: The Convener now gives his credentials: the throne itself, with every resource the search could need. Yisrael (H3478), 'he strives with God', names the covenant people over whom he reigned.

13.text: I set my heart to seek and to spy out by wisdom everything that is done under heaven. It is a sore business, this heavy task God has given the sons of man to be humbled by.
13.amp: I gave [natan] my heart [leb -- the inner man of mind and will] to seek [darash -- to study out] and search out [tur -- to explore as a scout spies out a land] by wisdom [chokmah] concerning all that is done [asah] under heaven [shamayim]: this sore [ra] travail [inyan -- task, business] God [Elohim] has given to the sons of man to be humbled [anah] by.
13.notes: darash (H1875) is to seek by study, and tur (H8446) is to scout or spy out a country; the Preacher explored life like unmapped territory. inyan (H6045), task or business, is another word unique to this book, and anah (H6031) means to afflict or humble: the search itself is the discipline.

14.text: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun, and look: everything is vapor, a chasing after wind, a grasping at what cannot be held.
14.amp: I have seen [raah] all the works [maaseh] that are done under the sun; and behold, all is vapor [hebel] and a chasing after wind [reuth ruach -- a shepherding of the wind, grasping at what no hand can hold].
14.notes: reuth (H7469), from a root meaning to shepherd or strive after, yields the KJV's 'vexation of spirit' and the modern 'chasing after wind' (ruach, H7307): herding the wind, the perfectly futile occupation.

15.text: What is bent cannot be straightened, and what is not there cannot be counted.
15.amp: That which is crooked [avat -- bent, twisted] cannot [yakol] be made straight [taqan -- set right]; and that which is lacking [chesron -- the deficit] cannot be numbered [manah].
15.notes: avat (H5791) is to bend or twist, and taqan (H8626), to set straight, appears only in Ecclesiastes; the world's warp is past human repair. chesron (H2642), the missing entry in the ledger, cannot even be tallied (manah, H4487).

16.text: I spoke with my own heart, saying, 'Look, I have grown great and gathered more wisdom than all who were before me in Jerusalem; my heart has seen for itself a great store of wisdom and knowledge.'
16.amp: I communed [dabar] with my own heart [leb], saying [amar], 'Look, I have become great [gadal] and increased [yasaph] in wisdom [chokmah] beyond all who were before [panim] me in Jerusalem; my heart has seen [raah] much [rabah] wisdom and knowledge [daat].'
16.notes: gadal (H1431), to become great, and yasaph (H3254), to add or increase: the credentials are real. The KJV margin notes that his heart 'had seen much' (raah, H7200) wisdom, knowledge won by firsthand experiment rather than hearsay.

17.text: So I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly as well, and I came to know that this too is a striving after wind.
17.amp: I gave [natan] my heart [leb] to know [yada] wisdom [chokmah], and to know madness [holelut] and folly [sikhluth]: I perceived that this also is a striving after wind [raayon ruach].
17.notes: He ran the experiment from both ends, chokmah (H2451) and its opposites, holelut (H1947), madness, and sikhluth (H5531), folly. raayon (H7475) is a twin of verse 14's reuth: still herding the wind.

18.text: For where wisdom multiplies, grief multiplies with it, and the man who adds to his knowledge adds to his pain.
18.amp: For in much [rob] wisdom [chokmah] is much grief [kaas -- vexation, sorrow with anger in it]: and he that increases [yasaph] knowledge [daat] increases sorrow [makob -- pain].
18.notes: kaas (H3708) is grief with provocation in it, vexation, and makob (H4341) is pain felt bodily deep. Knowledge under the sun grows both: the more clearly he saw, the more it hurt.
